- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3-5 days), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; reduce forecast peak by 5-10% and add a slight downward slope.
- If sentiment is positive but price is trending down, model often underestimates reversal; add a small upward bias (e.g., +1-2% in next 3-5 days) to reflect sentiment-driven recovery.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1-3 days) when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative — increase forecast by 1-3% for short-term (1-3 day) horizon.
- For 10+ day horizons, model tends to overestimate mean reversion; reduce forecast by 2-5% if sentiment is weak or neutral, to reflect persistent volatility.
- When sentiment is volatile (e.g., alternating +/– 0.3+), model often fails to capture momentum; use sentiment average over 3-5 days to smooth and anchor forecast.
